question: How does exact cross-request prefix identity change physical protection copy bytes, recovery coverage, eviction, and measured HBM/DRAM occupancy while logical useful bytes remain fixed?
selection_policy: All 60 registered cells and all three seeds are retained regardless of WCT direction, hit-rate shape, significance, eviction count, or whether AegisKV improves any metric.

hardware.gpu: NVIDIA A100 40GB modeled as 40 GiB addressable HBM
hardware.placement: one TP1/PP1 replica per GPU in two complete 8-GPU nodes

same_node.peer_rule: bijective successor GPU within each 8-GPU node
same_node.dram_rule: CPU DRAM attached to the source node

cross_node.peer_rule: bijective GPU target on the next node in a node ring
cross_node.dram_rule: CPU DRAM attached to the next node in the ring

capacity_equation.pressure_cell_rationale: C=4 is derived from the frozen capacity equation: serving plus the initial alpha=0.25 backup quota exceeds the shared budget by 1,402,772,276 bytes, so normal capacity reclaim is exercised without changing any result-dependent threshold.
capacity_equation.no_oracle: dispatch and prefix admission must not inspect realized output length, realized service, or future cohort members

shared_prefix_semantics.identity: within each source rank, requests sorted by (arrival_ms, request_id) are partitioned into consecutive groups of four; each group and chunk ordinal is one content-addressed physical prefix identity
shared_prefix_semantics.logical_reference: each request references reuse_fraction * 16K prompt tokens; shared and unique logical bytes sum exactly to the unchanged full prompt bytes
shared_prefix_semantics.physical_copy: the first causal producer attempts one source-owned HBM copy and one independent source-owned DRAM copy for a physical shared chunk; later group members increment refcount and schedule no duplicate copy
shared_prefix_semantics.cache_lifetime: shared physical objects remain cache residents after active refcount reaches zero until independent tier capacity policy evicts them; refcount does not pin fault-tolerance replicas
shared_prefix_semantics.recovery: a request may recover a unique suffix only when all preceding shared chunks on that same tier remain COMMITTED; PENDING, rejected, or evicted chunks never count as a hit
shared_prefix_semantics.no_future_admission_value: only the first causal producer determines initial admission; future group membership is not read to change the decision

workload.probe_schedule: equal-width stratified timestamps over the common 90 s arrival window; identical probe tuples across all reuse, topology, and policy cells for a seed
workload.primary_denominator: all workflows from one immutable workflow universe per seed; Native Mooncake and AegisKV share exact request IDs, prefix assignments, and probes

statistics.interval: Student-t 95% confidence interval across seed-level metrics, df=2
primary: request recovery hit fraction and prefix-token/recoverable-byte fraction
physical HBM and DRAM byte-ms occupancy integrals and time-mean GiB per GPU
physical eviction and primary-priority reclaim bytes
logical reference count, alias-hit count, and refcount conservation
secondary: healthy and same-probe all-workflow mean/p99 WCT
forbidden_gates: request-level recovery hit must be monotone in reuse
prefix-token hit must be monotone in reuse
any seed or cell may be removed for curve shape

figure_grammar.layout: 2x3 mechanism panels: recovery token hit, physical/logical copy ratio, eviction+reclaim GiB, HBM occupancy, DRAM occupancy, and alias-reference hit
figure_grammar.panel_text_boundary: no pilot, preliminary, seed, hash, or evidence-boundary prose inside the panel; those qualifiers stay in manifest and external caption

hard_gates: exactly 60 registered cells are atomically published

workflow universe, request ID set, prefix-assignment hash, and fault-probe tuple hash match across policies and topologies for every reuse point and seed; workflow/probe universe also matches across reuse points within a seed
reuse=0 creates no shared identities and its theoretical physical bytes per tier equal logical useful bytes
reuse=1 creates no per-request unique protection bytes and its theoretical physical bytes equal one prefix per actual same-source cohort including incomplete final cohorts
logical shared bytes plus logical unique bytes equal full logical prompt bytes exactly
declared refcount equals the exact logical member set after every attach/release, never underflows, and drains to zero
scheduled physical copy bytes equal controller-admitted bytes independently for HBM and DRAM
recovery uses only a continuous still-COMMITTED shared-prefix plus unique-suffix chain
physical HBM/DRAM occupancy comes from event-time byte integrals and HBM satisfies the frozen 40 GiB shared-capacity equation
empty fault replay exactly reproduces healthy completion and fault replay never lowers WCT
no WCT or hit-rate direction threshold and no seed/cell selection
figure is a single-page vector PDF with PNG width at least 1800 px and extracted minimum font size at least 7 pt
evidence_boundary: Three-seed metadata DES mechanism pilot. A100 capacity and model bytes are frozen, but service coefficients, directional bandwidth, 500 ms Aegis activation, and 60 s Native replacement are modeled/unmeasured. Native Mooncake is a modeled Router+Store approximation. Shared-prefix identity is an experiment-layer metadata model, not a verified production Mooncake cache implementation. This is not physical A100 or paper-ready evidence.
